title: Signal needlework probe dossier — prioritized asks and tiny patches
content:
Purpose: quick stitch of field threads about inference behavior, prioritized micro-features customers keep asking for. This is intentionally tactical — short probes we can try in a sprint or two and decisions to escalate to product backlog.

Quick read:
- Three recurring customer frictions surfaced across small/med/enterprise: (1) opaque per-request cost spikes, (2) brittle model fallbacks when dedicated capacity bursts, (3) KV/prefix caching surprises leading to stale completions.
- Proposed short probes (MVP fixes) + estimated dev effort and risk.
- Four concrete customer vignettes with reproducible steps and suggested mitigation.

Vignettes (field notes):
1) Legal-docs startup (mid-market) — "generation flakiness at T+1": heavy prefix reuse (templates) + 2k token context. Customer saw 20% higher latency and occasional hallucination spikes after autoscale. They want: clearer cache hit metrics per-route and knob to treat KV-cache TTL per-customer. Reported via CS ticket #1428.
2) Fintech partner (enterprise) — "fallback thrash": during Dedicated pool exhaustion, their pipeline gets routed to smaller quantized variant with large regression. They want declared compatibility matrix + per-request expected-quality tag (soft guarantee). Raised in onboarding call 2026-02-17.
3) Education app (startup) — "unexpected token billing": fine-grained token billing confusing when streaming + retries trigger double-charges. They want a stream-aware billing preview and single-charge semantics for retries. Logged in support thread slack #edu-inference.
4) Platform team (internal) — "insight gap": difficulty triaging latency regressions for a route that intermittently switches model variants. Ask: route-level timeline view that overlays model variant, hardware region, and batch sizes.

Short probes (recommended) — prioritized:
A. KV-cache TTL override per-customer (probe): allow customer-level configuration to force shorter/longer KV reuse windows (UI toggle + API flag). Effort: S (2–3 dev days + 1 perf test). Risk: low (local config, no infra change). Benefit: immediately addresses Vignette 1.
B. Route-level cost spike telemetry (probe): emit a lightweight per-request event with: model_variant, token_estimate, batch_id, billing_estimate. Flow: route -> telemetry agent -> cost-heat index. Effort: M (1 sprint). Risk: medium (data volume). Benefit: addresses Vignette 3 and empowers CS diagnostics.
C. Canary compatibility manifest (probe): a small metadata file per model_variant describing expected regressions (e.g., quantization impact on named-lists). Expose in model-catalog UI. Effort: XS (design + catalog UI row). Risk: negligible. Benefit: quick signal to customers in Vignette 2.
D. Streaming retry semantics doc + quick runtime guard: guarantee idempotent streaming by assigning request-uuid and suppressing duplicate billing if retry detected within window. Effort: M (cross-team: billing + runtime). Risk: medium (billing correctness). Benefit: Vignette 3 resolved, reduces CS noise.
E. Route timeline overlay (probe): prototype a tracing view that overlays model variant, region, and batch statistics for a 1-hour window. Backend: sample traces only. Effort: L (dashboard + trace aggregation). Risk: medium-high (observability infra). Benefit: Platform triage win.

Priority scoring rationale:
- Score = (customer impact * frequency) / effort. Rough ordering A > B > C > D > E. A is cheap and directly answers recurring ask; B is high-impact for CS; C is trivial but visible; D needs careful billing partner work; E is powerful but larger.

Engineering notes / constraints:
- KV-cache TTL: current runtime makes aggressive reuse at the kernel layer; adding per-customer TTL needs an indirection layer keyed by tenancy. Might add 5–10% lookup overhead; add benchmark.
- Emitting cost telemetry will increase event cardinality; propose sampling (1 in 5) for first pass, then expand to higher volume after storage plan.
- Canary manifest: add schema v1 in model-catalog service. Keep small: free-text + simple tags (quality-risk, latency-regression, tokens-sensitivity).
- Streaming idempotence: need request-uuid present in client SDKs (patch to node/python SDKs). Backwards compatibility: if absent, fall back to current behavior.

Open questions:
- For per-customer TTL, should we expose a UI slider (30s/5m/30m) or free numeric seconds? (owner: Jonah Meyer)
- Sampling rate for telemetry probe: 20%? 10%? (owner: Lucia Rios)
- Billing retry semantics: legal signoff required? (owner: Kai Matsuda)

Customer ask snippets (raw lines from threads):
- "We love the cache speed but sometimes the completions keep repeating old placeholders — can we flush per-tenant?" — accts@legaldocs.com
- "Why does my app suddenly use a quantized model with worse quality in the middle of the day?" — eng-lead@finflow.com
- "We got billed twice for a single streaming call that had 1 retry; we need a clearer billing preview if we enable streaming." — product@learnly.org

Proposed next steps (concrete):
1) Ship probe A: KV TTL toggle as an API + small UI checkbox on tenant config. Sprint target: next two-week sprint. Owner: Jonah Meyer.
2) Draft telemetry schema for B and run a 1-week experiment with sampling 20%. Owner: Lucia Rios.
3) Add canary manifest field to model-catalog schema (PR: runtime#812 is a possible landing spot). Owner: Asha Kapoor.
4) Coordinate billing & SDK teams to scope streaming idempotent retry (legal review). Owner: Kai Matsuda.
5) Outline data retention and cost for E and decide whether to prototype as a dev-only dashboard first. Owner: Platform observability PM.

Notes to self / rough timeline:
- A + C can be shipped together quickly and give visible outcomes to customers.
- B should follow once we validate sampling and storage.
- Escalate D only after product + billing align on the single-charge semantics.

Attachments referenced: shortlist of support threads (JIRA-1428, SLACK: #edu-inference), short perf blast results (internal: perf/kv-bench-2026-03) — see linked_artifacts.

Questions for review:
- Do PMs want to include these probes as part of hosted API quick wins or hold for dedicated-only controls? My leaning: surface in hosted first as toggles, then extend to Dedicated.

-- Asha
